purpose: Coverage inventory, not a pass report or unchanged-upstream execution claim. Every function in these nineteen locked suites is classified; 642 reference parameter cases are not 642 candidate passes. Private helpers/backend hooks/SQL traces/cache/locks, backend variants, open metadata/introspection gaps and BSON/client/diagnostic/configuration/clock-allocation differences are explicit.

Submillisecond input changes normalize to identical BSON milliseconds, leaving update/replace modified counts zero. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

UserDict/OrderedDict materialize recursively through separate clients; mutating a returned object cannot mutate stored data or another client's result. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

Both parameterized dict and UserDict aliases materialize root/nested documents as their origin types. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

SON materialization is checked recursively with BSON available, not skipped. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

Real async PyMongo find/clone/to_list/aggregate/distinct/find-and-modify preserve recursive OrderedDict and aware datetimes. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

Ordering, counts, input indices and caller-owned op objects are checked. BriskDB deliberately keeps server diagnostics payload-free: keyPattern/keyValue and interpolated index/key errmsg values are absent, not fabricated. Five reference backends do not imply five BriskDB backends.
Real installed-wheel wire traffic checks accepted IDs, rejected input indices and original operation identity, including mixed ID/secondary-key/missing-key conflicts.

The local helper checks serialization before any insert even beyond 1,000 documents, with ordered/unordered and validation-bypass variants. Generated input IDs survive rejection and no namespace is created. Driver InvalidDocument text is retained, not TinyMongo's custom collection/index/path message format; no transaction or storage-error atomicity is promised.
The actual async PyMongo client shares eager preflight, return IDs, partial duplicate counts and input error indices.
Empty/non-document input, nonboolean ordered and a late failing iterator are rejected before mutation. Empty generators are also rejected explicitly.

Tuple/generator and UserDict input preserves caller IDs, embedded boolean/number identity, explicit null uniqueness, result objects and records across reopen. Caller RawBSONDocument IDs keep stock PyMongo's omission from inserted_ids.
Public scalar-ID update/delete does not target an array-ID record; BriskDB does not share TinyDB's physical storage implementation.
The wire normalizes tuples and lists to the same BSON array identity; the second insert is a duplicate and the first survives.

Excluded private implementation assertions: monkeypatched Python backend find/commit/physical-key functions, fabricated racing engines and exact retry/encoding call counts are not BriskDB APIs. Linked real-wire tests cover public duplicate/counter/identity/concurrency results and client custom encoders once, not the reference's private retry count or native storage optimization.

TinyMongo's fallback errors module when PyMongo is absent is not applicable to the opt-in BriskDB client, which explicitly requires pinned PyMongo. The real PyMongo BulkWriteError shape is exercised; no fallback class is shipped.

TinyMongo's private dynamic/fallback validator-name catalog and monkeypatches do not apply. BriskDB delegates validation to its required pinned PyMongo constructor; it does not publish that helper or a no-PyMongo replacement. Public rejection before storage is checked for both real clients.

The public tinymongo_folder alias is accepted by BriskDB's MongoClient/AsyncMongoClient and persists in that folder. BriskDB stores its own manifest/shards, not TinyDB app.json files, and does not expose TinyMongo private _foldername state or its separate TinyMongoClient classes.

BriskDB requires a single folder option even when aliases have equal values; conflicting aliases also reject. TinyMongo-only threads/duckdb_config and foreign backends are rejected, not silently accepted or advertised as BriskDB backend implementations.
The real async default client constructs and closes; BRISKDB_HOME is isolated to a temporary test root so the test cannot create user data.

Both real client constructors reject malformed document/timezone/unknown options before native acquisition. New roots stay absent and existing stores are not opened or recovered; additional cross-pool validation is covered.
All source falsey document classes and timezone input forms are checked in both sync and async clients with the driver's actual codec settings.
Unknown options fail eagerly as PyMongo ConfigurationError for the public BriskDB clients; TinyMongo's separate TinyMongoClient TypeError class/message is not emulated.

Retained timeout, pool, retry, appName, listener, selector and server_api options use real PyMongo validation. Remote hosts/credentials are deliberately replaced by the owned local endpoint; construction and actual database traffic verify the binding.
Owned installed-wheel scenarios exercise the public behavior through real PyMongo. This is an adapted scenario, not unchanged execution of TinyMongo's private implementation.

Sorting uses complete source fields before projection. Modern PyMongo indexing requires an unevaluated clone; TinyMongo's post-iteration integer/string indexing and current-record interface are not emulated.

Empty mappings/sequences and filter aliases return complete public documents. TinyMongo-only parent.database metadata and its capabilities dictionary are not BriskDB client interfaces.
All eleven source conflict/code cases and seven unsupported expressions are checked against both existing and absent namespaces; invalid requests create no collection.

Local clients reject a bare string projection instead of silently treating it as characters. Non-string/NUL BSON field names fail with driver InvalidDocument rather than a private-helper TypeError/OperationFailure; other malformed containers/paths fail explicitly.

Nested array/scalar/missing-branch projection is checked through actual stored documents. The private project_document(None, spec) branch is represented by public find_one returning None, not claimed as the same implementation.
The same projection/filter/sort/skip outcomes are exercised before indexing, after index creation and after reopening BriskDB's own sharded store.

BSON-supported scalar, binary, embedded and array identifiers retain values and routes. Python 2**80 cannot cross BSON Int64 and fails before mutation; it is not claimed as a stored unbounded Python integer.
Owned installed-wheel scenarios exercise the public behavior through real PyMongo. This is an adapted scenario, not unchanged execution of TinyMongo's private implementation.

These inject failures into TinyMongo's private Python SQL compiler and inspect its private ID projector. BriskDB has neither hook; public scan/index/projection/count outcomes are covered, not a reproduced injected compiler branch.

Fake third-party Python backend classes, legacy hook signatures and override call counts do not apply to BriskDB's native storage architecture. Public projected sorting/windows are tested without claiming those hooks or plugin compatibility.

Single-result and exact-ID outcomes plus the source's mutated-after-find query isolation are checked. Local sync/async wrappers freeze nested filter/projection mappings. Private SQLite SQL strings/decode counts are not portable; native bounded work has separate engine/wire metrics tests.

Public first-match/filter/window/count results and bounded native count fanout are checked. BriskDB may use different physical reads and has no Python JSON decoder/SQL trace hook; exact source SQL/decode counts are not asserted.
Skip/limit/sort/clone/rewind/close/alive behavior is covered. Empty iteration is used instead of TinyMongo-only has_next/hasNext helpers; modern PyMongo cursor behavior remains explicit.
Async public single-result, bounded list and count behavior survives reopening. The source's Python decoder monkeypatch and exact pushdown counts are implementation-specific and not reproduced.

The same 64 x 100KB public-read comparison checks Python-client tracemalloc peaks and exact projected/count/first/full results. This measures the client heap only, not Rust allocations, engine RSS or sustained-load memory bounds.
Top-level/nested/missing fields, single/multi matched/modified counts, no-op repetitions and restart persistence are tested in BriskDB; TinyMongo's five backend variants are not BriskDB backends.
Async unset results, no-op counts and exact post-images survive reopening the native store; no claim of implementing the reference's five Python backends.

Public logical names/handles/drop/reopen and unaffected neighbor databases are exercised. Full list_databases statistics remain an explicit code-115 gap under #166; nameOnly=True is supported, not fabricated sizeOnDisk/empty fields. Modern list_database_names replaces the removed database_names alias. BriskDB shares native shard files; TinyDB JSON, named-memory and Parquet-directory deletion/zero-size assertions are not its layout or backend contracts.
Public sorted selection, projection, deletion and missing-match results are checked through the installed wheel; three reference backends are not three candidate backends.

Distinct/index metadata, lazy reads, clone/negative limit, partial to_list, rewind and exhaustion are covered. BriskDB exports its warning as briskdb.mongo.IndexCompatibilityWarning. Pinned real PyMongo cursors retain buffered rows after close and allow rewind; TinyMongo's permanent-close rejection and strict boolean cursor-argument behavior are not promised. No TinyMongo cursor replacement or private cache is installed.
Consumed position and repeat exhaustion are tested using real one-row wire batches, not a standalone TinyMongo in-memory cursor constructor.
Old/new images, sorted updates, projection, update/replacement upserts and invalid return_document values are exercised without replacing driver methods.

TinyDB's monkeypatched _acquire_collection_lock counts (three/two Python acquisitions) do not exist in the native SQLite engine. Public mutations and competing writes are exercised separately; they are not evidence for identical private lock counts or cross-shard transactions.
Embedded-document ID mutation counts and exact stored identity are checked after reopening native storage.

Dotted children, bracket/private-name access, separate namespaces and typo errors are checked, plus local input snapshots and reopen. Error classes match; messages name real PyMongo types rather than TinyMongo types. Reference backend variants are not BriskDB backends.
The corresponding async dotted-child, private-name, independent read and typo behavior is tested with the real PyMongo async client; message class names and backend variants remain as above.

TinyMongo's private _databases cache, monkeypatched constructor count and same-object identity are not PyMongo's handle model. Eight synchronized selectors check equivalent logical handles, one owning client, no implicit catalog writes and visibility through every selected collection instead. This does not claim a shared Python object cache.
Mutating returned read/write concern dictionaries cannot mutate later snapshots or another concern view.

Real competing update_one/update_many/replace_one operations on one shared collection check matched counts and no lost increments; async competitors are also covered. TinyMongo's build_table monkeypatch/single-build-call assertion has no native counterpart. These are bounded single-record tests, not global atomicity or a sustained soak claim.

On supported Linux/macOS shared-root lock hosts, six spawned processes each own a BriskDB client/listener and insert 50 generated-ID records; parent checks all exit codes, exact 300 values/unique IDs after reopen, with bounded joins and owned-child cleanup. Other platforms explicitly skip this host-dependent test. Unlike TinyDB implicit creation, schema is created before overlapping native roots because shared-root DDL admission is explicitly separate. No inherited native runtime, retry masking, unbounded soak or cross-process schema-creation claim.

Wire failures preserve existing records and reject invalid increments with code 14 even without a match. Unsupported operators surface as real PyMongo WriteError rather than TinyMongo's private TinyMongoNotSupportedError hierarchy; no cross-document transaction claim.

Isolated native atomic-clock tests cover repeated/backward seconds, rollover, terminal exhaustion and 512 concurrent unique allocations. Wire tests cover direct-zero stamping while preserving IDs, nested values and inputs. TinyMongo monkeypatch globals, Python object identity for private no-op helpers and optional _TIMESTAMP=None are not native APIs.

Ordered/unordered stored results, original error-operation identity and monotonic timestamps are checked. BriskDB reserves stamps during full-batch native preflight: an unattempted ordered tail can leave extra timestamp gaps (same-second first/after delta 3 here, versus TinyMongo's per-attempt delta 2). Exact monkeypatched wall-clock values and identical allocation counts are not claimed.

Driver BSON encoding rejects the invalid record before any write or clock allocation. The next valid record is monotonic and same-second allocations remain adjacent. TinyMongo's InvalidDocument.document identity/enriched diagnostic context is not a guaranteed PyMongo wire-client error surface.

BriskDB stores native BSON rather than exporting TinyMongo's private tagged-JSON codec. Exact native BSON bytes and returned types for bounds, timestamp and JavaScript are checked; TinyMongo JSON tag output is not claimed.
Nested scoped JavaScript, timestamp, bounds and plain JavaScript preserve exact native BSON and Python types. TinyMongo's private JSON envelope layout is not the native storage/serialization API.
All 20 malformed tag lookalikes round-trip as ordinary user BSON. The runtime does not invoke TinyMongo's private JSON decoder; this is not an offline tagged-JSON import claim.

TinyMongo monkeypatches individual optional private codec classes. BriskDB has no such tagged-JSON codec globals: SQL-only wheel operation without bson/pymongo and explicit failure when requesting document conversion without bson are checked by an isolated import-blocking process. Mongo clients require the pinned PyMongo extra.

Public equality filters and distinct compare encoded BSON identity, distinguishing timestamps, bounds, strings, JavaScript, scoped code and scope order. TinyMongo private registry keys/spec names/hashes are not exposed.
All 15 type ranks are exercised via whole-value push sorting and exact encoded BSON, not field-sort array-minimum semantics. Private Python registry tuple ranks are not an exposed API.
Native Python regex insertion round-trips as PyMongo bson.Regex with the same pattern/flags, not TinyMongo's re.Pattern reconstruction. The driver representation difference is asserted explicitly.
OrderedDict reads preserve unscoped Code type and scope=None, as well as scoped/nested counterparts.
Code rename destinations are rejected with WriteError code 2 without record changes.
Code count output fields are rejected with code 40156, preserving the original data.
Code index names are rejected with real PyMongo OperationFailure, not TinyMongo's custom unsupported exception hierarchy; no index/catalog change is allowed.
Scalar and paired Code index fields fail with the pinned driver's TypeError, not TinyMongo's custom unsupported exception. Existing records and index metadata are unchanged.
Both commands reject Code values with code 14, preserving the selected index and data.
Scalar, paired and find-keyword Code sort fields all raise TypeError through the local real-driver cursor path.

Nested non-BSON scope values raise InvalidDocument and never write a record. BriskDB retains the driver's error surface, not TinyMongo's enriched collection/ID/path message or error.document identity.
Real wire queries distinguish regex execution against strings/arrays, exact stored regex identity and explicit equality; stored option differences remain significant.
Membership, all/not and empty-all results are checked over scalar and array records through the authoritative native matcher.
Valid imsxu/zero-embedded flags and exact 51108/2/51075 option-conflict codes are checked. Private validator entry points and diagnostic strings are not exposed.
Locale-flagged regex matches only its exact stored BSON identity, not string predicate execution.

All 15 source cases reject without creating collections. BSON-serializable malformed queries retain source error codes. Regex cstrings containing NUL or invalid UTF-8 fail as driver InvalidDocument/InvalidStringData before transmission. Real PyMongo cursors validate server query semantics when consumed, not eagerly at find construction; private storage-read hooks are not claimed.
Direct, $regex and explicit equality forms preserve locale regex identity, leaving same-text strings unmatched.
TinyMongo's partial regex-only validator is a private optimization hook. BriskDB has no such public API; PyMongo find(None) uses the ordinary empty-filter path.

All 18 source contexts are represented: malformed predicates reject with exact codes, nested literal regex values are not compiled, and malformed BSON regex cstrings fail in the driver before transmission. One authoritative full matcher is used, not two private Python validation passes.

No partial-validator bypass is exposed. The real wire frontend rejects malformed $in/$elemMatch shapes with code 2 even though TinyMongo's private regex-only fast preflight intentionally ignores them.
Operator documents inside $in/$nin/$all regex arrays reject with code 2 before implicit catalog creation.

TinyMongo's Remote SQL backend rejection hook does not exist in BriskDB's native SQLite engine. A real native unique index instead checks UUID/subtype-4 binary equivalence and duplicate code 11000. This is not a claim to implement TinyMongo's external SQL-backend policy or support its runtime backend plugins.

Recursive numeric identity deduplicates 1/1.0 while preserving bool separation. Arbitrary Python equality objects returned by a mocked TinyMongo collection cannot enter native BSON and are rejected by the driver. Representative numeric encoding/order is not promised across native shard traversal.

All 29 source argument cases reject before implicit catalog creation. BSON-serializable arguments retain exact server codes; non-string keys and out-of-int64 integers instead fail driver encoding as InvalidDocument/OverflowError. Private storage-open hooks are not exposed.
Unsupported metadata sorting rejects without catalog creation through a real PyMongo OperationFailure, not TinyMongo's custom unsupported exception/message.
Integral float sort/skip/limit arguments produce the expected page without changing the caller pipeline.
Signed-int64 maximum skip/limit are accepted. An explicit ID sort avoids promising shard-natural ordering.
Empty counts emit no row; filtered counts feed later projection.
Mixed-direction compound sorting is deterministic with an explicit ID tiebreaker, and mutations of returned nested values do not alter stored documents.
Native aggregation preserves code 16746 for ambiguous numeric paths and code 2 precedence for parallel arrays.
Two sorts around skip/limit preserve pipeline-stage ordering.

TinyMongo's direct Python aggregation/cursor helpers warn on arbitrary non-BSON values. Those private hooks do not exist in the native engine; date/object inputs fail driver encoding. Public ascending/descending array min/max is checked separately, not a claim to reproduce private warning counts.

Public aggregate sorting checks scalar ancestors, out-of-bounds numeric paths, and array min/max. Native sort keys are not the private Python tuple representation; arbitrary objects cannot be encoded.

The public 1000-element shared-array result is checked alongside the bounded native sorter regression. TinyMongo's monkeypatched exactly-2000 Python call count is not a native API/performance promise.
Inclusion, exclusion, nested specifications and ID flag modes retain exact results.
Computed ID, nested renames, literals and missing references evaluate against the original input.
Top-level and nested BSON field ordering is checked explicitly, not merely dict equality.
Computed dotted outputs retain recursive array shapes, scalar conversion, empty arrays and missing shells.
Include-only branches omit scalar array elements and scalar ancestors even alongside computed branches.
Numeric/boolean/path/document/tuple-array literals are not evaluated as expressions; caller pipeline remains unchanged.
Generic subtype decodes as bytes while custom binary subtype is retained.
REMOVE produces missing fields/shells, null expression-array elements and literal text when explicitly quoted.
REMOVE dotted suffixes remain missing in projection and set operations.
Ordinary field references do not recursively traverse nested arrays.
Both aliases accept empty no-ops and evaluate assignments from the original input without changing stored values.
Nested set updates traverse objects/scalars/arrays and preserve empty containers.
BriskDB has no direct Python aggregation engine helper; equivalent public BSON tuple encoding and nested-array transformations are checked without mutating caller inputs.
Nested object specifications update paths, while literal/empty object values replace the whole value.
REMOVE deletes leaves while retaining or creating shells through scalar/array paths.
String/list/tuple unset forms preserve exclusion semantics including scalar array members.
All 30 source error cases plus both invalid set aliases retain exact Mongo codes and create no collection. Private backend-read hooks and diagnostic wording are not a public contract.
All five unsupported expression/variable/numeric-path cases reject before catalog creation as wire OperationFailure code 115, not TinyMongo's custom unsupported exception.
All five REMOVE suffix errors and earlier path/expression precedence cases retain exact codes before catalog creation.
Non-string BSON output keys raise PyMongo InvalidDocument during encoding rather than TinyMongo's TypeError; no collection is created.
Async composition uses a real PyMongo AsyncCommandCursor and explicit ID sort; TinyMongo's cursor class and implicit natural ordering are not promised.
Real PyMongo CommandCursor supports iteration/context cleanup but has no clone/rewind API. Returned nested values and caller pipelines remain isolated; rerunning aggregation is not a snapshot clone.

Numeric equality groups 1/1.0 separately from bool; arrays and ordered documents retain BSON identity. Missing dotted groups map to null and array references skip absent members. Unsorted cross-shard group order/representative numeric encoding is not promised.
Arbitrary Python object members cannot enter BSON and fail driver encoding, not TinyMongo's private helper None/custom-error policy. Public ordered-document group identity is checked separately.

All four non-list pipeline forms reject as TypeError. A trailing null stage fails pinned PyMongo's own stage inspection as TypeError; the other three malformed stage shapes fail server validation. None create a collection.
Unsupported lookup rejects before catalog creation. Empty-pipeline identity is tested through real wire execution instead of the private direct Python engine.

Public leading and post-group matches preserve stage semantics. Native routing tests prove safe leading-ID pruning and preservation of the original pipeline; TinyMongo's monkeypatched collection.find call counts do not exist.
Computed fields use original input, retain default/special ID rules, omit missing values and preserve stored documents/pipelines.
